newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cavallo faces trial for calling judge "corrupt".
newsitem.headline: Cavallo faces trial for calling judge "corrupt".

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo will have a public hearing before a federal court on Nov. 14 for calling a Supreme Court judge corrupt, a court said on Wednesday.

Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco told reporters he decided to put Cavallo in the dock after his attempt at a legal retraction earlier this week was thrown out. "I didn't consider the content to be sufficient," said Bagnasco.

The case dates back to 1993, when Cavallo called Supreme Court judges Augusto Belluscio and Enrique Petracchi "corrupt thieves" for their ruling in a case against the Central Bank. Both sued, but Petracchi accepted a retraction last month.

Cavallo's lawyers filed a retraction on Monday admitting the irascible ex-minister made the comments "without personally checking the quality of the information I had and whether it was complete and accurate."
But Belluscio rejected this as a "light" excuse instead of an unconditional apology. "He did not take back what he said or admit he gravely offended my honour," said the judge.

Cavallo, widely praised for beating hyperinflation and fostering growth while minister, has whipped up a political storm since his firing by continuing his crusade against corruption and accusing two ministers and President Carlos Menem's top aide.
They deny the charges and are threatening legal action, while another Argentine judge is fighting Cavallo in court over corruption allegations.
Cavallo, asked recently in Brazil whether he plans to run for president in 1999, answered with defiant humour: "I don't think I'll be president because they'll put me in jail first."
